[1] [Relocation > Relocation / Address Change > Importance of Communicating Location > Long-Term Relocation > Eligibility to Work]
If you are interested in a long-term relocation (defined above), you need to confirm that you would be eligible to work in that location. [Except for the Netherlands](/handbook/people-group/visas/#right-to-immigrate-to-the-netherlands), GitLab does not provide any form of sponsorship or immigration aid for team members who choose to move to new countries. For more information, please refer to our [Visa page](/handbook/people-group/visas/). GitLab cannot assist or facilitate a process to help you become eligible to work in a location if you do not already have that eligibility. You are of course free to apply and gain that eligibility if there are steps you can take that do not involve GitLab.  Once you are certain that you are eligible to work in your requested location country, you will need to provide proof of eligibility by [uploading the proof in the Documents tab of your Workday profile](https://docs.google.com/document/d/19B0lsMu7dMhof1ghPuBxHP23DuDqi2qpWF8pCWyEUN4/edit). If you move before establishing eligibility to work, but then cannot establish eligibility to work in the new location within the first six months of residency, it may affect your ability to continue your role with GitLab.

[2] [GitLab France S.A.S. > We've Got You Covered > Time Off Policies > Sick Leave Policy]
When illness strikes, GitLab provides comprehensive sick leave support through a combination of French social security benefits and company salary supplementation, ensuring financial stability during health challenges.

Eligibility Requirements

First 6 months of sick leave:

- 150 hours worked in prior 3 months, OR
- Salary of 1,015 times hourly SMIC in prior 6 months

Beyond 6 months:

- 12 months of social security contributions
- 600 hours worked in prior 12 months, OR
- Income of 2,030 times hourly SMIC in prior 12 months

Coverage & Key Features

- Up to 6 months sick leave (extendable based on eligibility)
- GitLab supplements social security to provide 100% salary for first 25 working days
- After 25 days: Social security benefit of 50% daily wage (max €50.58/day)
- [Review current sick time policies](https://employment-social-affairs.ec.europa.eu/policies-and-activities/moving-working-europe/eu-social-security-coordination/your-rights-country-country/france_en)

How to Report Sick Leave

1. Notify GitLab within 48 hours via "Out Sick" in Workday
2. Send sheet no. 3 from physician to leaves@gitlab.com
3. Submit sheets no. 1 & 2 to social security organization
4. For extensions: Notify within 48 hours with updated sheet no. 3

Important Details

- Notification deadline: 48 hours
- Medical documentation required
- GitLab salary supplement: First 25 working days

Contact Information

Sick leave reporting and policy questions: leaves@gitlab.com

[3] [GitLab BV (Netherlands) Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Time Off Policies > Sick Leave Support]
Comprehensive coverage when you're unable to work due to illness.

Leave Entitlement

* 100% salary for first 25 days
* 70% salary continuation for up to 104 weeks total
* GitLab complies with [Dutch local laws](https://business.gov.nl/regulation/reporting-employee-illness-recovery/) regarding sick leave. Local laws override any leave policy we have in the benefit of the team members

How to Report

* Select "Out Sick" in Workday

Employees of GitLab B.V. have further rights and responsibilities regarding sick time based on Dutch law, as written into their employment [contracts](https://internal.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/people-operations/people-operations/employment_contracts/):

Question: If I move from GitLab B.V. in the Netherlands to GitLab France S.A.S., how does the salary coverage for the first 25 days of sick leave differ between the two countries?

Answer:
Based on the provided context, there is **no difference** in the salary coverage for the first 25 days of sick leave between the two entities.

*   **GitLab France S.A.S.**: The policy states that GitLab supplements social security to provide **100% salary** for the first 25 working days.
*   **GitLab B.V. (Netherlands)**: The policy states that employees receive **100% salary** for the first 25 days.

In both cases, the employee receives 100% of their salary for the initial 25 days of sick leave.

Is every factual claim in the answer directly supported by the passages? Reply with one word: Yes or No.
